summary: This bill amends the Federal Deposit Insurance Act to raise the cap on reciprocal deposits that insured banks may hold without them counting as brokered deposits, setting tiered limits at 50% of liabilities up to $1 billion, 40% of liabilities from $1-10 billion, and 30% of liabilities from $10-250 billion, expands eligibility to banks with CAMELS ratings of 1-3, requires an FDIC study on reciprocal deposit performance since 2018, and offsets costs by cutting the Federal Reserve's surplus fund by $28 million in 2036.

scores.thoughts: Section 5 reduces the Federal Reserve's Discretionary Surplus Fund by $28 million (effective 2036). This is a minor, one-time reduction in available federal financial resources, which tangentially relates to government spending by slightly constraining funds.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, or revenue collection.
No provisions address healthcare policy, coverage, or markets.
No provisions relate to firearms, regulations, or rights.
No provisions address immigration, borders, or related protections.
No provisions address reproductive rights or abortion access.
No provisions address military or defense spending.
No provisions address environmental regulations or climate policy.
No provisions address welfare programs or social safety net benefits.
No provisions address schools, education funding, or choice programs.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related policy.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
No provisions address trade, tariffs, or globalization.

The minor reduction to the Federal Reserve surplus fund in Section 5 has a negligible, tangential effect on fiscal resources that could relate to debt management, but the impact is too small and delayed to register meaningfully.
No provisions address LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
No provisions address foreign aid or international assistance.
No provisions address voting access, election integrity, or reforms.
No provisions address technology regulation, data privacy, or oversight.
No provisions address labor rights, unions, or employer flexibility.
No provisions address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination laws.
